summary: When Erev Pesach falls on Shabbos, some parts of the korban Pesach are done anyway, and some must wait. This mishnah lists which are which.

chunks.he: אֵלּוּ דְבָרִים בַּפֶּסַח דּוֹחִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
chunks.en: These things of the korban Pesach push aside Shabbos:
chunks.explain: They are done even on Shabbos.
chunks.st: These are the matters related to the Paschal lamb that override Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: when the eve of Passover occurs on Shabbat:

chunks.en: shechting it, throwing its blood, cleaning
chunks.st: Its slaughter, the sprinkling of its blood, the cleaning of

chunks.en: its insides, and burning its fats.
chunks.explain: These must be done while it is still day.
chunks.st: its intestines and the burning of its fats on the altar, all of which are services that must be performed on Passover eve while it is still day.

chunks.en: But roasting it and rinsing its insides
chunks.st: However, its roasting and the washing of its intestines, which need not be done by day,

chunks.en: do not push aside Shabbos.
chunks.explain: They can wait until after Shabbos.
chunks.st: do not override Shabbat; rather, one waits until after Shabbat to perform these tasks.

chunks.en: Carrying it, and bringing it from outside the techum,
chunks.st: Carrying the Paschal lamb through a public domain does not override Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: The Paschal offering consisted of either a lamb or a goat, sometimes quite young and unable to walk the entire way, so that it had to be carried on a person’s shoulders.

words.note: How far one may walk out of town on Shabbos.

chunks.en: and cutting off its wart,
chunks.st: Similarly, bringing it from outside the Shabbat limit and cutting off its wart

words.note: A bump on its skin that makes it unfit.

chunks.en: do not push aside Shabbos.
chunks.explain: They could have been done before Shabbos.
chunks.st: do not override Shabbat, as all these tasks could have been performed before Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: A wart is considered a blemish that disqualifies the animal from being brought as an offering, but once the wart is removed, the animal is fit to be sacrificed on the altar.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says, they do push it aside.
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says: All of these procedures override Shabbat.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva argue whether Rabbinic Shabbos rules are pushed aside for the korban Pesach. In the end, Rabbi Akiva gives a rule: what could be done before Shabbos does not push Shabbos aside.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said:

chunks.en: isn't it logical?
chunks.st: Could this not be derived through an a fortiori inference?

chunks.en: If shechting, which is forbidden as
chunks.st: If slaughter, which is ordinarily forbidden on Shabbat

chunks.en: real work, pushes aside Shabbos,
chunks.explain: Work the Torah forbids on Shabbos.
chunks.st: as a biblically prohibited labor, nonetheless overrides Shabbat when performed for the sake of the Paschal lamb, then

chunks.en: these, which are only Rabbinic rules,
chunks.st: these activities, namely carrying the animal, bringing it from outside the Shabbat limit, and the like, which are prohibited due to rabbinic decree,

words.note: A Shabbos rule made by the Rabbis.

chunks.en: shouldn't they push aside Shabbos?
chunks.st: should they not override Shabbat?

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

chunks.en: Yom Tov will prove it is not so:
chunks.st: The law governing a Festival proves otherwise,

chunks.en: they allowed real work on it,
chunks.st: for the Torah permitted on it acts that are normally prohibited as labor, such as slaughtering, cooking, and baking,

chunks.en: but Rabbinic rules are forbidden on it.
chunks.st: and yet it is forbidden to do on it acts that are prohibited due to rabbinic decree.
chunks.stMore: Thus, we cannot derive policy with regard to rabbinic prohibitions from the rules that govern Torah laws.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:

chunks.en: What is this,
chunks.st: What is this,

chunks.en: Yehoshua? How can something you may choose prove about a mitzvah?
chunks.st: Yehoshua? How can you suggest such a weak proof? What proof can be deduced from optional activities that would apply to a mitzva?
chunks.stMore: How does the fact that rabbinic decrees remain in effect on a Festival with respect to optional activities prove that one is also forbidden to transgress a rabbinic decree in order to fulfill the mitzva of offering the Paschal lamb?

words.note: Something you don't have to do.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva answered and said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva responded and said in defense of Rabbi Yehoshua’s opinion:

chunks.en: sprinkling will prove it:
chunks.st: Sprinkling the purifying water of a red heifer upon someone who had contracted ritual impurity through contact with a corpse proves the matter,

words.note: Of the water of the parah adumah, to become tahor.

chunks.en: it is for a mitzvah, and it is only a Rabbinic rule,
chunks.st: for it is done for the sake of a mitzva, in order to allow the person to offer the Paschal lamb, and it is prohibited only due to rabbinic decree, and

chunks.en: and still it does not push aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: nonetheless it does not override Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: for the purification rite is not performed on the eve of Passover that falls on Shabbat.

chunks.he: אַף אַתָּה אַל תִּתְמַהּ עַל אֵלּוּ,
chunks.en: So you too, don't be surprised about these,
chunks.st: So, too, you should not be surprised about these activities, namely carrying the animal, bringing it from outside the Shabbat limit, and cutting off its wart,

chunks.en: that even though they are
chunks.st: that although they are performed

chunks.en: for a mitzvah and they are only Rabbinic rules,
chunks.st: for the sake of a mitzva and they are prohibited only due to rabbinic decree,

chunks.en: they do not push aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: they do not override Shabbat.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to him: I do not accept this proof.

chunks.en: about that I also say:
chunks.explain: Sprinkling should push aside Shabbos too.
chunks.st: With regard to this sprinkling itself, I infer that it, too, is permitted for the same reason:

chunks.he: וּמָה אִם שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁהִיא מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכָה,
chunks.en: if shechting, which is real work,
chunks.st: If slaughter, which is a biblically prohibited labor,

chunks.en: pushes aside Shabbos,
chunks.st: overrides Shabbat,

chunks.en: sprinkling, which is only a Rabbinic rule,
chunks.st: is it not right that sprinkling the purifying water of a red heifer, which is prohibited only due to rabbinic decree,

chunks.en: isn't it logical that it pushes aside Shabbos?
chunks.st: should override Shabbat?
chunks.stMore: You cannot challenge me based on a premise with which I disagree.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Eliezer:

chunks.en: or the other way around:
chunks.st: Or perhaps we can reverse the order of your argument and say the opposite:

chunks.he: מָה אִם הַזָּאָה שֶׁהִיא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת,
chunks.en: if sprinkling, which is only a Rabbinic rule,
chunks.st: If, as we know by accepted tradition, sprinkling the purifying water on Shabbat, which is prohibited only due to rabbinic decree,

chunks.en: does not push aside Shabbos,
chunks.st: does not override Shabbat, then

chunks.en: shechting, which is real work,
chunks.st: with regard to slaughter, which is prohibited as a biblically prohibited labor,

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁלֹּא תִדְחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
chunks.en: isn't it logical that it should not push aside Shabbos?
chunks.st: is it not right that it should not override Shabbat?
chunks.stMore: Therefore, it should be prohibited to slaughter the Paschal lamb when the eve of Passover occurs on Shabbat.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:

chunks.en: Akiva, you have uprooted what is written in the Torah:
chunks.st: Akiva, how can you say this? You have thus uprooted what is written in the Torah: “

chunks.en: "in the afternoon, at its set time" (Bamidbar 9),
chunks.st: Let the children of Israel offer the Paschal lamb in its appointed time” (Numbers 9:2);
chunks.stMore: the phrase “at its appointed time” indicates that the offering must be brought on that day,

chunks.en: whether on a weekday or on Shabbos.
chunks.st: whether it is a weekday or Shabbat.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Eliezer:

chunks.he: רַבִּי, הָבֵא לִי מוֹעֵד לָאֵלּוּ כַּמּוֹעֵד לַשְּׁחִיטָה.
chunks.en: "Rebbi, bring me a set time for these like the set time for shechting."
chunks.explain: The animal could be brought before Shabbos.
chunks.st: My teacher, bring me an appointed time stated in the Torah for these tasks, namely, carrying the animal or bringing it from outside the Shabbat limits, like the appointed time stated with respect to slaughter.
chunks.stMore: The Paschal lamb must be slaughtered on the fourteenth of Nisan, but there is no fixed time when the animal must be brought to the Temple, and it is therefore possible to transport it before Shabbat.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said a rule:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva stated a principle:

chunks.he: כָּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: any work that can be done before Shabbos
chunks.st: Any prohibited labor required for the offering of the sacrifice that can be performed on the eve of Shabbat

chunks.en: does not push aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: does not override Shabbat;

chunks.he: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: Shechting, which cannot be done before Shabbos,
chunks.st: slaughter, which cannot be performed on the eve of Shabbat,

chunks.en: pushes aside Shabbos.
chunks.st: overrides Shabbat.

summary: Sometimes an extra korban called the chagigah was brought together with the korban Pesach. This mishnah teaches when it was brought.

chunks.en: When does one bring a chagigah with it?
chunks.st: When does one bring a Festival peace-offering with the Paschal lamb?
chunks.stMore: A special offering is brought on the fourteenth of Nisan together with the Paschal lamb

chunks.en: When it comes on a weekday,
chunks.st: when the Paschal lamb comes on a weekday rather than on Shabbat,

chunks.en: when it is tahor, and when there is only a little.
chunks.explain: Many people share the korban Pesach, so each one gets just a little.
chunks.st: and when it comes in a state of ritual purity as opposed to when it is brought in a state of impurity because most of the community is impure, and when many people are registered for the Paschal lamb so that each person will receive only a small portion from it.
chunks.stMore: When these three conditions are met, the Festival peace-offering is eaten first and the Paschal lamb is eaten afterward.

chunks.en: But when it comes on Shabbos,
chunks.st: When, however, the Paschal lamb comes on Shabbat,

chunks.en: or when there is a lot, or when it is tamei,
chunks.st: or when few people are registered for it so that each person will receive a large portion, or when it is brought in a state of ritual impurity,

chunks.en: we do not bring a chagigah with it.
chunks.st: one does not bring a Festival peace-offering with it.

summary: This mishnah teaches which animals may be brought for the chagigah, and how long it may be eaten.
stIntro: With regard to the extra offering itself, the

chunks.en: The chagigah could come from the flock,
chunks.st: Festival peace-offering would come from the flock,

chunks.en: from the cattle,
chunks.st: from the herd,

chunks.en: from sheep and from goats,
chunks.st: from sheep or from goats,

chunks.en: from males and from females.
chunks.st: from males or from females,
chunks.stMore: as the Festival peace-offering is not bound by the limitations governing the Paschal offering, which must be specifically a young male sheep or goat.

chunks.en: And it is eaten for two days and one night.
chunks.st: And the Festival peace-offering is eaten for two days and one night like other peace-offerings.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua argue about someone who shechted a korban on Shabbos by mistake for the wrong purpose: does he have to bring a chatas?

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that he shechted not for its own sake on Shabbos,
chunks.st: A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered for a different purpose on Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: not knowing that it is prohibited for him to do so, is disqualified, and

chunks.en: he must bring a chatas for it.
chunks.explain: He did forbidden work on Shabbos by mistake.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin-offering for it
chunks.stMore: because he unwittingly performed a prohibited labor on Shabbat.

words.note: A korban for doing a sin by mistake.

chunks.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשׁוּם פֶּסַח,
chunks.en: And all other korbanos that he shechted as a korban Pesach,
chunks.st: As for all other offerings, such as a peace-offering, that one unwittingly slaughtered on Shabbat for the purpose of a Paschal offering,

chunks.en: if they can't be a korban Pesach,
chunks.st: if they were not fit for the Paschal offering, e.g., if they were female or cattle or more than a year old and clearly ineligible for the Paschal offering,

chunks.en: he must bring one. And if they can be,
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin-offering. Because he did not fulfill the mitzva to bring a Paschal offering, his act of slaughter was therefore unnecessary. And if they were fit,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says he must bring a chatas,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer nevertheless deems him liable to bring a sin-offering for his unwitting transgression.

chunks.en: and Rabbi Yehoshua says he does not.
chunks.explain: He meant to do a mitzvah, and he did do a mitzvah.
chunks.st: But Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him,
chunks.stMore: because he maintains that if someone intended to perform a mitzva, and despite his error he in fact performed a mitzva, he is not liable to bring a sin-offering. And in this case he performed a mitzva, because offerings that are sacrificed for a different purpose are still fit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.he: מָה אִם הַפֶּסַח שֶׁהוּא מֻתָּר לִשְׁמוֹ,
chunks.en: if the korban Pesach, which may be shechted for its own sake,
chunks.st: If, with regard to the Paschal lamb, which is permitted to be slaughtered on Shabbat for its own purpose,

chunks.en: when he changed its name,
chunks.st: when one changed its purpose he is

chunks.en: he must bring one, other korbanos, which are forbidden even for their own sake,
chunks.explain: Other korbanos may not be shechted on Shabbos.
chunks.st: nevertheless liable, then, with regard to other offerings that are forbidden to be slaughtered on Shabbat even for their own purpose,

chunks.en: when he changed their name,
chunks.st: when one changed their purpose,

chunks.en: isn't it logical that he must bring one?
chunks.st: is it not right that he should be liable?

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

chunks.en: No. If you say so about the korban Pesach,
chunks.st: No, this reasoning is faulty. If you say that one is liable to bring a sin-offering if he slaughtered a Paschal lamb for a different purpose, it is

chunks.en: that he changed it to something forbidden,
chunks.st: because he changed its purpose for something forbidden,
chunks.stMore: as the offering he intended it to be may not be slaughtered on Shabbat.

chunks.en: can you say so about other korbanos,
chunks.st: But can you necessarily say the same thing about other offerings that he slaughtered for the purpose of a Paschal offering

chunks.en: that he changed them to something allowed?
chunks.st: and thus changed their purpose for something that is permitted to be sacrificed on Shabbat?

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.en: the korbanos of the community will prove it,
chunks.st: Let the communal offerings, such as the daily offering and the additional-offerings of Shabbat and the Festivals, prove the matter,

words.note: Like the tamid and the mussaf.

chunks.en: which may be shechted for their own sake,
chunks.st: for they are permitted to be slaughtered on Shabbat for their own purpose,

chunks.en: and one who shechts another korban for their sake
chunks.st: and nevertheless, one who unnecessarily slaughters a different offering for their purpose

chunks.en: must bring a chatas. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: is liable.This indicates that even when a particular offering may be slaughtered, one is nevertheless liable if he slaughtered a different offering for the purpose of the permitted offering. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

chunks.en: No. If you say so about the korbanos of the community,
chunks.st: No, if you say this halakha with regard to communal offerings,

chunks.en: which have a set number,
chunks.st: it is because they have a limit,
chunks.stMore: as there is a specific number of communal offerings that must be offered on any particular day and there is no reason one would mistakenly sacrifice extra offerings for this purpose.

chunks.en: can you say so about the korban Pesach, which has no set number?
chunks.st: But can you necessarily say the same thing about the Paschal lamb, which does not have a limit, making it more likely for someone to make a mistake?

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: אַף הַשּׁוֹחֵט לְשֵׁם אֵמוּרֵי צִבּוּר, פָּטוּר:
chunks.en: even one who shechts for the korbanos of the community is free.
chunks.st: According to Rabbi Yehoshua, even one who unwittingly slaughters other offerings for the purpose of communal offerings beyond their daily limit is exempt for the same reason, i.e., that he intended to fulfill a mitzva that is permitted on Shabbat.

summary: This mishnah teaches when someone who shechted a korban Pesach on Shabbos, and it turned out not to be kosher, must bring a chatas.
stIntro: The mishna continues with another halakha with regard to the Paschal lamb:

chunks.en: If he shechted it not for those who will eat it and not for those signed up for it,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered a Paschal lamb on Shabbat and mistakenly intended it for those who cannot eat it, such as sick or elderly people who are unable to eat the meat, or for those who did not register for it,

chunks.en: for people without a bris or for people who are tamei,
chunks.st: or for the sake of the uncircumcised or for those ritually impure,

chunks.en: he must bring a chatas. For those who will eat it and for those who won't,
chunks.st: the offering is disqualified and he is liable to bring a sin-offering for his unnecessary act of slaughter. If, however, he slaughtered it for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it,

chunks.en: for those signed up and for those not signed up,
chunks.st: or for those who registered for it and for those who did not register for it,

chunks.en: for those with a bris and for those without,
chunks.st: or for the circumcised and for those who are uncircumcised,

words.en: and for those without a bris

chunks.en: for those who are tahor and for those who are tamei,
chunks.st: or for those who are ritually impure and those who are ritually pure,

chunks.en: he is free. If he shechted it and it turned out to have a mum,
chunks.explain: The korban is still kosher, so his shechting was allowed.
chunks.st: he is exempt. Since a Paschal lamb slaughtered with dual intentions of these types is valid, the act of slaughter was justified. If he slaughtered it and it was found to have a blemish, the offering is disqualified, and

words.note: A flaw that makes an animal unfit for a korban.

chunks.en: he must bring one. If he shechted it and it turned out to be a hidden tereifah,
chunks.explain: He should have checked the animal for a mum first.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin-offering for having unwittingly performed a prohibited labor on Shabbat, as he should have examined the animal before it was slaughtered. If he slaughtered it and it was found to have a hidden condition that would cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa] and that could not have been discovered before the slaughter even if it were examined properly, the offering is disqualified, but

words.note: An animal with a sickness that makes it not kosher.

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. שְׁחָטוֹ וְנוֹדַע שֶׁמָּשְׁכוּ הַבְּעָלִים אֶת יָדָם,
chunks.en: he is free. If he shechted it and then found out that the owners had pulled out,
chunks.explain: Nobody could have known about the hidden sickness.
chunks.st: he is exempt from bringing a sin-offering. This is not a case of shogeg, unwitting violation of Shabbat, but rather of ones, an unavoidable accident. If he slaughtered it and afterward it became known that the owners had withdrawn from it and registered for a different Paschal lamb, in which case this one was slaughtered unnecessarily, as no one was registered for it,

chunks.en: or that they died or became tamei,
chunks.st: or it became known that they had died or became ritually impure,

chunks.en: he is free, because he shechted with permission.
chunks.st: in all these cases he is exempt from bringing a sin-offering, because he slaughtered with permission.
chunks.stMore: At the time of the slaughter, he did not know and had no reason to suspect that the offering would be disqualified.
